newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends higher on spillover.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends higher on spillover.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled higher on spillover support from the closing rally in CBOT and KCBT wheat futures, traders said.
"All day long, Minneapolis led Kansas City and Chicago. Toward the close, soybeans started firming up on fund-buying and then KCBT and CBOT wheat surged. We just followed," a MGE floor trader said.

There was speculation that the rally may have come on talk that logistical problems in Canada had caused some foreign buyers to opt to buy U.S. spring wheat. But some traders doubted that this had been a major factor Tuesday.

"We've been hearing rumors for some time that existing Canadian sales might be loaded out of U.S. ports, but I can't imagine why anyone would be forced to come to us to buy wheat," a trader said. "Europe is still cheaper than us."
MGE spring wheat settled two to 5-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 5-3/4 cents at $3.88-1/4.

Traders said commercial spreading was a feature during the session. The MGE March/May spread began trading as narrow as 15-1/2 cents per bushel but widened out to 18 cents before closing at about 17 cents.
MGE barley settled one cent per cwt lower to five cents higher, with March down one cent at $6.50.
